title: test(scripts): batch 7 pilot — floor check-sdui-manifest on its own table row labels
body:
Part of #13799

**Batch 7 PILOT — one file, `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs`**, the smallest of the ten table-driven `scripts/**` self-tests, under **recipe A** decided in `5537261715` / `5537301204`. The pilot exists to settle the shape the other nine copy, so the shape decisions are stated here as a spec rather than left to be read off the diff.

`failures === 0` was this self-test's only success condition, so "every case held" and "the cases never ran" printed the same line.

## Why the sink cannot carry the floor here

The file is table-driven: one literal `cases` table, one loop over it, and a sink (`failures++`) that writes **only when a case fails**. Routing that sink through `registerCase()` would register a case only on failure — a fully green run would register 0 and every battery would read DID NOT RUN. That is the floor inverted, not installed. Batch 4's thunk route is no escape for this class either (four of the sibling files carry `continue` in the loop body, which cannot cross a function boundary).

## The shape, for the next batch to copy verbatim

**1. Battery name = the row label, verbatim.** The labels already exist in the source as the table's first column, so no authoring judgement is needed, and a refusal line quotes exactly the string a reader greps for. No prefix is added: a prefix would have to be re-derived by every future reader to match a refusal against a row.

**Two rows sharing a label are refused at declaration time**, by two halves that each hold on their own and were each measured:

- a duplicate written into the **roster literal** collapses to ONE key, so the roster falls below its pinned size — `SELF_TEST_BATTERIES declares 5 batteries, below the pinned 6`;
- a duplicate written into the **table** leaves the roster whole, so a cross-check reads the row labels directly and names WHICH label collided — `the cases table uses "missing record is RED" as a row label more than once`.

A shared label would otherwise be one battery for two rows, so the second row could stop running while the first keeps the floor met.

**2. `registerCase(name)` is the first statement of the driving loop body**, attributing the case to the row actually being run, whatever that row asserts afterwards. There is no `battery()` opener: for a table-driven self-test the ROW *is* the battery, so attribution is the loop variable rather than a most-recently-opened section. A per-iteration helper call is already a landed shape (`check-doc-frontmatter`, `check-test-source-alias`).

**3. The roster is a LITERAL the table is checked against — never derived from the table.** A derived roster pins nothing: a deleted row would delete its own floor in the same edit. Each row label maps to floor **1**, the honest number for a table row (the loop reaches it exactly once per run), and the floors stay floors rather than equalities so a row that grows into several registrations does not red. The roster's own size is pinned at the row count, because deleting an entry silences a floor exactly as effectively as zeroing it.

⛔ No assertion condition touched. ⛔ No control flow rewritten — no `continue` to `return`, no thunk around the loop body, no comment promoted to a section head. The verdict handshake (`SELF_TEST_VERDICT`) is kept exactly as landed. The two `continue` statements added live in the new floor block's own loops; the driving loop still has none.

One deliberate text change, reachable only on a red run: the failure line reads `N failure(s) (cases and floor)` rather than `N case(s) failed`, because floor breaches are counted in the same sink as case failures and the old wording would have mis-named them. The **green** line is byte-identical to the base (below).

## Verification record

Base worktree at the dispatch pin `460134af8`, installed, for the byte comparisons. Branch head `fbb42081e`.

| what | reading |
|:--|:--|
| surface | exactly 1 file (three-dot vs `origin/main`), +107/−1; `skip-changeset` (a `scripts/**` gate publishes from no package) |
| `--self-test` | exit 0 — `6 cases behave (green passes; absence, tamper, moved pin, emptiness are RED).` |
| normal mode | exit 0 — `sdui.manifest.json is present, intact (sha256 49211fee7792…, 57 components) and fresh at objectui pin 00d3f09c500c…` |
| stdout + stderr vs base | all four streams **byte-identical** (`cmp` silent; `--self-test` stdout sha256 `6c949991bc56…` on both trees, normal-mode stdout `449c7ea7428d…` on both) |
| case count, measured on runs | 6 before, 6 after. Roster size pinned to an unreachable 7 reads `declares 6 batteries, below the pinned 7`; a single row's floor raised to 2 reads `registered 1 case(s), below its pinned floor of 2`, so each row registers exactly once and six rows are declared — 6 registrations, matching the `${cases.length}` the verdict prints |
| `extractWatchHints` | identical on both trees, and empty on both — this gate declares no path population. Structural, not incidental: admission is `/^[\w.@][\w.@/*-]*$/` over the raw literal, and every row label contains spaces, so no roster key or row label can ever be admitted as a path hint (checked directly against all six labels: all six rejected) |
| census | `node scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs --json`: NONE **45 to 44**, ROSTER 122 to 123, COUNT 2 unchanged — a drop of exactly 1, and the symmetric difference of the two classifications is `scripts/check-sdui-manifest.mjs` alone |

**Ablations.** The implementation was committed before any leg, so the restore had a real reference point. Every mutation is proven on disk by an anchored count plus the blob hash moving off the HEAD blob; every restore by `git checkout HEAD -- path` then hash equality against the HEAD blob **and** an empty `git diff HEAD`; every leg carries a `trap` restore on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths. Two legs were refused by their own landing check when my anchor assertion miscounted — those are non-measurements, re-run rather than reported as passes.

| leg | reading |
|:--|:--|
| (a) delete one row from the table | exit 1, naming THAT row: `self-test battery "moved pin is RED" DID NOT RUN — 0 cases registered, 1 pinned` |
| (b) rename a row's label | exit 1, naming BOTH halves: `"moved pin is AMBER" registered 1 case(s) but is not declared in SELF_TEST_BATTERIES`, and `"moved pin is RED" DID NOT RUN` |
| (c) remove the `registerCase()` call | exit 1, all **6** rows DID NOT RUN, and not one `✗ self-test:` case line printed — every original case still passes while the self-test now refuses |
| (d) roster size pin unreachable | exit 1, `declares 6 batteries, below the pinned 7` |
| (e) one row's floor raised to 2 | exit 1, `registered 1 case(s), below its pinned floor of 2` |
| (f) duplicate label in the table | exit 1, naming the collided label, plus the displaced row as DID NOT RUN |
| (g) duplicate key in the roster | exit 1, `declares 5 batteries, below the pinned 6`, plus the now-undeclared row |

## Gates

Derived family from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`, all run in the foreground, plus the always-runs tail and a control-byte scan. Exit codes captured by redirect before any pipe; verdicts quoted from each gate's own line. The full record is in the `os-dev-report` comment on #13799.
